ideas.pitch: A Python and Wireshark-plugin network forensics tool that automatically reconstructs multi-step exfiltration payloads from packet captures during a CTF.
ideas.title: PCAP-Inspector
ideas.why_it_could_win: Tackles the digital forensics and network PCAP analysis domain by automating complex manual steps, reflecting hard engineering similar to past technical winners.

ideas.pitch: An automated cryptographic puzzle solver for custom asymmetric ciphers, small RSA exponent attacks, and common padding oracles encountered in CTF challenges.
ideas.title: CryptoForge Analyzer
ideas.why_it_could_win: Addresses the cryptography and steganography domain directly with algorithm-heavy execution, aligning with the pattern of winning hard engineering projects.

ideas.pitch: A static binary analysis companion that identifies custom calling conventions and common buffer overflow gadgets in stripped ELF binaries during reverse engineering challenges.
ideas.title: Binary-Guard Decompiler
ideas.why_it_could_win: Solves the reverse engineering and binary exploitation domain by automating vulnerability detection patterns judges look for in technical CTF puzzles.

ideas.pitch: A rapid payload testing environment tailored for complex server-side request forgery (SSRF) and deserialization vulnerabilities found in web exploitation tracks.
ideas.title: WebExploit Sandbox
ideas.why_it_could_win: Streamlines the web exploitation domain with an efficient, highly focused local testing harness that saves crucial minutes during a 6-hour sprint.

ideas.pitch: An OSINT framework that aggregates public social footprints, metadata, and infrastructure correlations into a visual node graph to uncover hidden system security flags.
ideas.title: OSINT Graph Mapper
ideas.why_it_could_win: Provides an edge in the OSINT and system security domain through graph intelligence and quick correlation, mirroring successful analytical platform architectures.
